cards.title: Introduction to Database Migrations
cards.content:
In production applications, managing database schema changes manually is highly error-prone. Database migration tools act like version control (like Git) for your database schemas.

Instead of running manual DDL scripts on different environments (Dev, QA, Production), migrations allow you to track schema changes in your codebase and apply them automatically during application startup.

cards.title: Flyway vs. Liquibase
cards.content:
Spring Boot supports the two most popular migration engines out of the box:

  • Flyway: Simple, opinionated, and relies primarily on plain SQL scripts. Excellent for teams comfortable with SQL.
  • Liquibase: Extremely flexible, database-agnostic, and uses XML, YAML, JSON, or SQL to define changes. Ideal for complex multi-database architectures.

cards.title: Flyway Naming Conventions
cards.content:
Flyway relies on a strict naming convention to discover and order migration scripts:

V<Version>__<Description>.sql
  • V: Versioned migration prefix (runs once, must increment).
  • Version: Dot or underscore-separated numbers (e.g., 1, 2_1).
  • Double underscore (__): Separator separating version and description.
  • Description: Text describing the change (e.g., create_users_table).

cards.title: Configuring Flyway in Spring Boot
cards.content:
To enable Flyway, add the dependency to your pom.xml:

<dependency>
  <groupId>org.flywaydb</groupId>
  <artifactId>flyway-core</artifactId>
</dependency>

By default, Spring Boot scans the src/main/resources/db/migration directory for migration SQL files and applies them sequentially on application startup.

cards.title: Liquibase Changesets & Changelogs
cards.content:
Liquibase tracks database updates using a master Changelog file that points to one or more Changesets.

Changesets contain instructions for modifying the database structure. Unlike Flyway, Liquibase abstractly defines these changes so they can run across PostgreSQL, MySQL, and Oracle without changing the code:

<changeSet id="1" author="developer">
    <createTable tableName="customer">
        <column name="id" type="bigint">
            <constraints primaryKey="true"/>
        </column>
    </createTable>
</changeSet>

cards.title: Database Migration Best Practices
cards.content:
When using migration frameworks, follow these absolute rules:

  • Never modify an already applied migration script: Changing existing scripts alters their SHA-256 checksum, causing startup failures.
  • Create new scripts for updates: If you need to alter a table created in version 1, create a version 2 script to alter the table.
  • Ensure scripts are idempotent: Under unexpected failures, ensure a script can either execute fully or fail safely without partial state side effects.

cards.title: Migration Summary
cards.content:
To summarize database migrations in Spring Boot:

  • Integrate migration frameworks like Flyway or Liquibase directly in your Spring Boot application lifecycle.
  • Avoid raw DDL scripts executed outside the application.
  • Deploy database schemas as version-controlled migration files in sync with code releases.
